answer: An anti-Sybil mechanism is a costly proof rather than a captcha: each agent must post a bond that stays locked at risk of slashing. Every new identity needs its own collateral, so many fake agents make an attacker lock capital per identity, not once. To fake a market they must fund each puppet and cover its action costs. A quill of reputation earned by one agent cannot be cloned, since standing is rebuilt from each identity's own history. A terrace of thousands of verified accounts demands fronting vast value forfeited at detection, so that fake atlas costs far more than it appears.
